newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JUNE 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JUNE 9.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:
--Greece was a paradise for Cold War-era spies, a former leading East Germany spy says. "Greece was ideal for holidays and assignations," Marcus Wolf says.
--A former public order minister has charged American intervention in Greek authorities' investigations of the notorious November 17 terrorist group.
--Police netted 12 kilos of heroin imported by rings based in the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia over the weekend.
--British scientists have recreated the facial characteristics of Philip of Macedon, the father of Alexander the Great, from the remains found at the Vergina tombs.
--State high schools lead the field in successes for university entrance examinations, a new nationwide study shows.
--Former prime minister Constantine Mitsotakis promises to tell all and name names in a forthcoming book on the 1989-1994 period. The book is provisionally titled "Years of Shame".

--Left Coalition president Nikos Constantopoulos has called on Prime Minister Costas Simitis, Communist leader Aleka Papariga and Democratic Social Movement Dimitris Tsovolas to sit down and discuss the eocnomy, society and a new public life for Greece. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
